blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Much of the most consequential work in a large organisation is done by people without the formal authority to make the decisions their work depends on. They must persuade, not command; co-ordinate, not instruct; bring others along rather than direct them. That condition sounds like a constraint, but in practice it is often the school in which the best executives are quietly trained.

Influence without authority rests on a few unglamorous foundations. The first is reliability: if your work is consistently high quality and on time, people begin to give you the benefit of the doubt on everything else. The second is reciprocity: if you routinely make other people's jobs slightly easier when nothing is at stake for you, they are disposed to return the favour later, when it is. The third is patience: influence compounds over quarters, not weeks.

Language is subtly different in this mode. A phrase heard as presumptuous from a peer — "we must move quickly" — lands very differently from someone without formal authority. The same idea, expressed as "I sense we may benefit from moving quickly, though I defer to your view", can carry the same substance while respecting the political reality. This is not weakness — it is craftsmanship.

items.q: According to the text, why is working without formal authority described as "the school in which the best executives are quietly trained"?
options: Because persuasion and coordination develop skills that command does not
Because it is a formal management programme
Because it avoids all political conflict
Because junior staff are always given authority later
items.why: "They must persuade, not command… bring others along." — a limitação força o desenvolvimento de habilidades reais de liderança.

items.q: What are the three foundations of influence without authority named in the text?
options: Reputation, incentives and structure
Speed, authority and hierarchy
Reliability, reciprocity and patience
Charisma, seniority and budget
items.why: "The first is reliability… The second is reciprocity… The third is patience."

items.q: Why does reciprocity work, according to the passage?
options: Because it is required by company policy
Because helping others when nothing is at stake makes them disposed to return the favour later
Because favours are formally tracked and repaid
Because people fear being reported to their manager
items.why: "make other people's jobs slightly easier when nothing is at stake… they are disposed to return the favour later."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Softening your language can preserve the substance of your point.
Formal authority is not required to shape important decisions.
Deferring to others is a sign of weakness that undermines influence.
Trust is earned gradually through consistent delivery.
items.why: Inferência: o texto conclui que essa forma de falar "is not weakness — it is craftsmanship".

items.q: The contrast between "we must move quickly" and "I sense we may benefit from moving quickly, though I defer to your view" suggests that…
options: urgency should always be avoided in meetings
form can matter as much as content when you lack formal power
peers are never allowed to give direct advice
the second speaker has less to contribute
items.why: Inferência: a mesma ideia é aceita ou rejeitada conforme o registro — a embalagem importa quando falta autoridade.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie conduzindo uma mudança que atravessa várias áreas — nenhum dos gerentes afetados se reporta a ela. Responda sem ler a transcrição; ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, a quick word on where we are — because I know none of you formally report to me, and I want to be honest about how I intend to work.

I am not going to walk into your teams and start reordering priorities. That is not my call, and frankly it would not stick even if I tried. What I would like instead is to understand where each of you stands before I propose anything at all. If there is a version of this change that makes your quarter harder, I would rather hear it now than discover it in the steering meeting.

Here is what I can offer in return. Where the migration touches your roadmap, my team will absorb as much of the work as we reasonably can — the data mapping, the testing, the tedious parts. You get the outcome; we carry the load. That is not a favour I am banking for later; it is simply how I would like us to operate.

On timing — I do sense we may benefit from moving before the year-end freeze, though I genuinely defer to those of you who know these systems better than I do. If you tell me the window is wrong, I will trust that. All I ask is that we decide together, and that once we decide, we actually follow through.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie explicitly acknowledge at the start?
options: That none of the managers formally report to her
That the change has already been approved by the board
That she will be reordering their team priorities
That she has more experience than they do
items.why: "none of you formally report to me, and I want to be honest about how I intend to work."

items.q: What does Sophie's team offer to do in return?
options: Report progress directly to the board
Take over the managers' teams entirely
Absorb much of the work — data mapping, testing, the tedious parts
Delay the migration until next year
items.why: "my team will absorb as much of the work as we reasonably can — the data mapping, the testing, the tedious parts."

items.q: How does Sophie frame the offer to carry the load?
options: As a favour she is banking to call in later
As a condition for their cooperation
As a decision already made by her manager
As simply how she would like the group to operate
items.why: "That is not a favour I am banking for later; it is simply how I would like us to operate."

items.q: What can we infer about why Sophie asks to hear objections "now rather than in the steering meeting"?
options: She does not trust the steering committee
She wants the managers to prepare a formal report
She wants to avoid being publicly contradicted and to surface problems early
She is not allowed to attend the steering meeting
items.why: Inferência: descobrir resistências cedo evita surpresas e protege a coalizão — típico de influência sem autoridade.

items.q: Which best describes Sophie's approach to the timing question?
options: She insists on her preferred deadline regardless of their view
She leaves the decision entirely to her own team
She refuses to commit to any timeline
She offers a view but genuinely defers to those who know the systems
items.why: Inferência: "I do sense we may benefit… though I genuinely defer" — propõe, mas cede a quem tem o conhecimento.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Her reliability earned her a seat at tables she had no title to attend." Reliability is…
options: a formal job grade
the ability to be counted on to deliver consistently
the willingness to take risks
the size of one's team
items.why: Reliability = confiabilidade: entregar com consistência, o que gera confiança.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "She built ___ by helping other teams long before she ever needed anything from them."
options: reciprocity
hierarchy
authority
compliance
items.why: Reciprocity = reciprocidade: o favor de hoje predispõe o outro a retribuir amanhã.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Before proposing anything, map the ___ — who wins, who loses, and who merely tolerates the change."
options: reporting line
org chart
stakeholder landscape
budget cycle
items.why: Stakeholder landscape = cenário de stakeholders: o mapa de interesses a navegar.

items.q: "Though she disagreed, she chose to defer to the head of engineering on the timeline." To defer to someone means to…
options: overrule their decision
report them to a superior
yield to their judgement out of respect
postpone the meeting with them
items.why: To defer to = deferir / ceder ao juízo de alguém, por respeito à sua competência ou posição.

items.q: Implicit authority is best described as…
options: the legal right to sign contracts
power written into the org chart
authority delegated in writing by a manager
influence granted informally through trust and track record
items.why: Implicit authority = autoridade implícita: peso conquistado pela reputação, não pelo cargo — mais durável que o poder explícito.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem ao conduzir mudanças sem autoridade formal. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "She spent months getting each manager to bring others along rather than forcing the change." To bring others along means to…
options: invite them to a meeting
win their buy-in so they move with you willingly
assign them extra tasks
escalate the issue above them
items.why: Bring others along = trazer os outros junto, conquistando adesão em vez de impor.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the proposed timeline." They…
options: forwarded it to the board
approved it immediately
rewrote it overnight
resisted or raised objections to it
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The steering committee still has to sign off on the plan." To sign off on means to…
options: quietly ignore
comment informally
formally approve
announce to the press
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Everyone agreed in the room, but nobody followed through." They…
options: changed the plan halfway
failed to carry it to completion
documented it poorly
delegated it upward
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Giving people the benefit of the doubt is earned over months and spent in seconds." To give someone the benefit of the doubt means to…
options: delegate a decision to them
demand proof before trusting them
keep a record of their mistakes
assume the best of them despite uncertainty
items.why: Benefit of the doubt = benefício da dúvida: presumir boa-fé quando não há certeza — capital de confiança que leva meses para construir.
